category: Hardware Manager Advanced: ILA/VIO Control, Flash, JTAG/XVC, IBERT & Programming Files
description: The rest of the in-system toolkit: full ILA capture/trigger control properties and data handling, VIO and System Monitor access, configuration-memory (flash) programming details, device boot/readback/verify and SVF generation, remote and virtual-cable (XVC) targets, JTAG-to-AXI transactions, IBERT/Serial I/O Analyzer eye scans, debug-core insertion parameters (trigger-in/out, advanced triggers, capture qualification), and the programming file formats (.bit/.bin/.rbt/.msk/.mcs/.prm/.svf/.pdi/.ltx).

tools.name: set_property CONTROL.DATA_DEPTH / CONTROL.TRIGGER_MODE / CONTROL.CAPTURE_MODE / CONTROL.WINDOW_COUNT (hw_ila capture setup)
tools.description: Run-time capture configuration of an ILA core in the Hardware Manager, set on the hw_ila object before run_hw_ila: CONTROL.DATA_DEPTH (samples per window, up to the C_DATA_DEPTH the core was built with), CONTROL.WINDOW_COUNT (number of capture windows, DATA_DEPTH x WINDOW_COUNT <= core depth), CONTROL.TRIGGER_POSITION (sample index within the window where the trigger sits), CONTROL.TRIGGER_MODE (BASIC_ONLY, ADVANCED_ONLY, TRIG_IN_ONLY, BASIC_OR_TRIG_IN, ADVANCED_OR_TRIG_IN), CONTROL.CAPTURE_MODE (ALWAYS or BASIC: store only samples matching the capture condition), CONTROL.TRIGGER_CONDITION and CONTROL.CAPTURE_CONDITION (AND/OR of the probe compare values), and CONTROL.TRIG_OUT_MODE (DISABLED, TRIGGER_ONLY, TRIG_IN_ONLY, TRIGGER_OR_TRIG_IN) for cross-triggering.
tools.usage:
set_property CONTROL.DATA_DEPTH 1024 [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]
set_property CONTROL.WINDOW_COUNT 4 [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]
set_property CONTROL.TRIGGER_POSITION 256 [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]
set_property CONTROL.TRIGGER_MODE BASIC_ONLY [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]
set_property CONTROL.TRIGGER_CONDITION AND [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]
set_property CONTROL.CAPTURE_MODE BASIC [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]
set_property CONTROL.CAPTURE_CONDITION OR [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]
set_property CONTROL.TRIG_OUT_MODE TRIGGER_ONLY [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]

parameters.name: CONTROL.DATA_DEPTH
parameters.description: Samples per window: power of two up to the synthesized C_DATA_DEPTH.

parameters.name: CONTROL.WINDOW_COUNT
parameters.description: Windows per run; each window re-arms the trigger.

parameters.name: CONTROL.TRIGGER_POSITION
parameters.description: 0 = trigger at the first sample (only post-trigger data); DATA_DEPTH-1 = only pre-trigger data.

parameters.name: CONTROL.TRIGGER_MODE
parameters.description: Basic (compare values), advanced (state-machine trigger from a .tsm file: CONTROL.TRIGGER_STATE_MACHINE_FILE), or trigger-in based.

parameters.name: CONTROL.CAPTURE_MODE / CAPTURE_CONDITION
parameters.description: ALWAYS stores every sample; BASIC stores samples satisfying the capture compare values combined with AND/OR (requires C_EN_STRG_QUAL).

tools.example:
set ila [get_hw_ilas -of_objects [current_hw_device] -filter {CELL_NAME =~ "u_ila_axi"}]
set_property CONTROL.DATA_DEPTH 4096 $ila
set_property CONTROL.TRIGGER_POSITION 1024 $ila
set_property TRIGGER_COMPARE_VALUE eq1'b1 [get_hw_probes s_axi_awvalid -of_objects $ila]
set_property CAPTURE_COMPARE_VALUE eq1'b1 [get_hw_probes s_axi_wvalid -of_objects $ila]
set_property CONTROL.CAPTURE_MODE BASIC $ila
run_hw_ila $ila
wait_on_hw_ila $ila
display_hw_ila_data [upload_hw_ila_data $ila]
tools.notes: Properties are only accepted if the core was built with the feature (C_ADV_TRIGGER for ADVANCED, C_EN_STRG_QUAL for BASIC capture, C_TRIGIN_EN/C_TRIGOUT_EN for TRIG_IN/TRIG_OUT). The GUI's Settings tab of the ILA dashboard sets exactly these properties; reset_hw_ila returns the core to defaults.

tools.name: set_property CAPTURE_COMPARE_VALUE / TRIGGER_COMPARE_VALUE syntax (hw_probe compare values)
tools.description: The compare-value language used on hw_probe objects: <operator><width>'<radix><value> where the operator is eq, neq, lt, gt, lte, gte (numeric compares need C_PROBE_MUX/comparator type set at insertion) and for single bits the transition operators R (rising), F (falling), B (both edges) and N (no transition); radix b/h/o/u/d (unsigned/signed decimal with C_PROBEn_TYPE), X for don't care bits (e.g. eq8'hXX_1X), and multiple probes combine according to CONTROL.TRIGGER_CONDITION. CAPTURE_COMPARE_VALUE uses the same syntax for capture qualification. DISPLAY_RADIX sets the waveform radix per probe.
tools.usage:
set_property TRIGGER_COMPARE_VALUE eq1'bR [get_hw_probes start -of_objects $ila]      ;# rising edge
set_property TRIGGER_COMPARE_VALUE eq32'hDEAD_BEEF [get_hw_probes data -of_objects $ila]
set_property TRIGGER_COMPARE_VALUE gt16'u1000 [get_hw_probes count -of_objects $ila]   ;# numeric (needs comparator support)
set_property TRIGGER_COMPARE_VALUE eq4'b1XX0 [get_hw_probes state -of_objects $ila]    ;# don't-cares
set_property CAPTURE_COMPARE_VALUE eq1'b1 [get_hw_probes valid -of_objects $ila]
set_property DISPLAY_RADIX HEX [get_hw_probes data -of_objects $ila]

parameters.name: eq / neq / lt / gt / lte / gte
parameters.description: Comparison operators; the ordering ones need probes inserted with a comparator type other than 'equal' (Set Up Debug > Probe type) and C_PROBEn_MU_CNT.

parameters.name: R / F / B / N
parameters.description: Edge operators for 1-bit probes.

parameters.name: X
parameters.description: Don't-care digit in binary/hex/octal values.

parameters.name: DISPLAY_RADIX
parameters.description: BINARY, HEX, OCTAL, UNSIGNED, SIGNED: per-probe display radix in the waveform.

tools.example:
# Trigger when a write to address 0x4000_0000 occurs with a specific data value
set_property CONTROL.TRIGGER_CONDITION AND $ila
set_property TRIGGER_COMPARE_VALUE eq32'h4000_0000 [get_hw_probes s_axi_awaddr -of_objects $ila]
set_property TRIGGER_COMPARE_VALUE eq1'b1        [get_hw_probes s_axi_awvalid -of_objects $ila]
run_hw_ila $ila
tools.notes: Underscores in values are ignored. Enumerated display: add_hw_probe_enum / remove_hw_probe_enum attach names to values for state machines. Probe widths in the .ltx must match the design programmed; a stale .ltx gives 'probe width mismatch' errors.

tools.name: read_hw_ila_data / current_hw_ila_data / write_hw_ila_data -csv_file / -vcd_file
tools.description: Handling captured ILA data outside the live session: write_hw_ila_data stores an upload (from upload_hw_ila_data) as a native .ila file, or with -csv_file / -vcd_file exports the samples to CSV or VCD for spreadsheets and third-party viewers; read_hw_ila_data reloads a .ila file into a hw_ila_data object that display_hw_ila_data shows in the waveform viewer without any hardware attached; current_hw_ila_data / get_hw_ila_datas manage the data objects in memory.
tools.usage:
write_hw_ila_data [-csv_file <f.csv>] [-vcd_file <f.vcd>] [-legacy_csv_file <f>] [-force] [-quiet] <file.ila> <hw_ila_data>
read_hw_ila_data [-quiet] <file.ila>
display_hw_ila_data [-wcfg <file.wcfg>] [-reset] [-quiet] [<hw_ila_data>]
current_hw_ila_data [<hw_ila_data>]
get_hw_ila_datas [-of_objects <hw_ilas>] [-filter <expr>] [<patterns>]

parameters.name: -csv_file / -vcd_file
parameters.description: Also export the capture as CSV (one row per sample, columns per probe) or VCD.

parameters.name: -wcfg (display)
parameters.description: Waveform configuration to apply (probe order, radix, groups).

parameters.name: -force
parameters.description: Overwrite existing files.

tools.example:
set data [upload_hw_ila_data $ila]
write_hw_ila_data -force -csv_file ./capture_[clock seconds].csv ./capture.ila $data
# offline analysis on another machine (vivado_lab is enough)
set d [read_hw_ila_data ./capture.ila]
display_hw_ila_data -wcfg ./ila_axi.wcfg $d
tools.notes: The .ila file includes probe names and widths so it is self-contained. VCD export uses the ILA sample clock as time base (one time unit per sample). Very deep captures (megasamples with wide probes) take a while to upload over JTAG; consider a smaller DATA_DEPTH for iterative debug.

tools.name: get_hw_vios / set_property OUTPUT_VALUE / commit_hw_vio / refresh_hw_vio / reset_hw_vio_outputs
tools.description: Virtual Input/Output core control: get_hw_vios returns the VIO cores on the device, the input probes are read with refresh_hw_vio (updating INPUT_VALUE, with activity indicators for changing signals), and outputs are set by writing OUTPUT_VALUE on the output probes followed by commit_hw_vio, which pushes all pending values to hardware at once; reset_hw_vio_outputs restores the initial values from the core parameters and reset_hw_vio_activity clears the activity counters. Used for run-time control (resets, enables, test modes) and status readout without any processor.
tools.usage:
get_hw_vios [-of_objects <hw_devices>] [-regexp] [-filter <expr>] [-quiet] [<patterns>]
refresh_hw_vio [-update_output_values] [-quiet] <hw_vios>
set_property OUTPUT_VALUE <value> [get_hw_probes <probe> -of_objects <hw_vio>]
commit_hw_vio [-quiet] <hw_vios_or_probes>
reset_hw_vio_outputs [-quiet] <hw_vios>
reset_hw_vio_activity [-quiet] <hw_vios>
get_property INPUT_VALUE [get_hw_probes <probe> -of_objects <hw_vio>]

parameters.name: OUTPUT_VALUE
parameters.description: Value for an output probe, entered in the probe's DISPLAY_RADIX (e.g. 1 or 0 for a 1-bit probe, A5 for an 8-bit hex-radix probe).

parameters.name: INPUT_VALUE / INPUT_VALUE_ACTIVITY
parameters.description: Read-back value and activity (U/D/B/N) of input probes after refresh_hw_vio.

parameters.name: -update_output_values
parameters.description: Read the current output-probe values from hardware instead of assuming the last committed.

tools.example:
set vio [get_hw_vios -of_objects [current_hw_device] -filter {CELL_NAME =~ "u_vio"}]
set_property OUTPUT_VALUE 1 [get_hw_probes soft_rst -of_objects $vio]
commit_hw_vio $vio
after 100
set_property OUTPUT_VALUE 0 [get_hw_probes soft_rst -of_objects $vio]
commit_hw_vio $vio
refresh_hw_vio $vio
puts "link_up = [get_property INPUT_VALUE [get_hw_probes link_up -of_objects $vio]]"
tools.notes: VIO outputs are synchronous to the core's clock; a stopped clock means the write never takes effect (the GUI shows a warning). The VIO dashboard in the GUI is the interactive equivalent with LEDs, buttons and text fields per probe.

tools.name: get_hw_sysmons / refresh_hw_sysmon / get_property TEMPERATURE / set_hw_sysmon_reg
tools.description: Read the on-chip System Monitor (XADC/SYSMON) through JTAG without any design support: get_hw_sysmons returns the monitor object(s), refresh_hw_sysmon samples it and updates properties such as TEMPERATURE, VCCINT, VCCAUX, VCCBRAM, VCCO_DDR (family dependent), plus MIN/MAX statistics, and the register-level commands get_hw_sysmon_reg / set_hw_sysmon_reg access the DRP registers (e.g. to change the sequencer or alarm limits). The Hardware Manager dashboard plots the same values over time.
tools.usage:
get_hw_sysmons [-of_objects <hw_devices>] [-regexp] [-filter <expr>] [-quiet] [<patterns>]
refresh_hw_sysmon [-regexp] [-properties <list>] [-quiet] <hw_sysmons>
get_property TEMPERATURE <hw_sysmon>
get_hw_sysmon_reg <hw_sysmon> <hex_address>
set_hw_sysmon_reg <hw_sysmon> <hex_address> <hex_value>
commit_hw_sysmon <hw_sysmons>

parameters.name: Properties
parameters.description: TEMPERATURE, TEMPERATURE_MIN/MAX, VCCINT, VCCAUX, VCCBRAM, VCCPINT/VCCPAUX/VCCO_DDR (Zynq), VUSER0..3 (UltraScale+), plus ALARM flags.

parameters.name: -properties
parameters.description: Refresh only the listed properties (faster polling).

parameters.name: register addresses
parameters.description: 0x00 temperature, 0x01 VCCINT, 0x02 VCCAUX, 0x40-0x42 configuration, 0x50+ alarm limits (see UG480/UG580).

tools.notes: Available even with no bitstream loaded (the monitor is always powered). Versal exposes SYSMON via the same commands with more supply rails; raw ADC codes convert with the family-specific formulas.

tools.name: set_property PROGRAM.ADDRESS_RANGE / PROGRAM.FILES / PROGRAM.PRM_FILE / PROGRAM.ERASE / PROGRAM.CFG_PROGRAM / PROGRAM.VERIFY / PROGRAM.CHECKSUM / PROGRAM.BLANK_CHECK (hw_cfgmem)
tools.description: The properties that drive configuration-memory programming on a hw_cfgmem object created with create_hw_cfgmem: PROGRAM.FILES lists the .mcs/.bin image(s) (two for dual-QSPI), PROGRAM.PRM_FILE the matching .prm map, PROGRAM.ADDRESS_RANGE selects use_file (only the image's range) or entire_device, and the boolean steps PROGRAM.ERASE, PROGRAM.CFG_PROGRAM, PROGRAM.VERIFY, PROGRAM.CHECKSUM and PROGRAM.BLANK_CHECK choose which operations program_hw_cfgmem performs; PROGRAM.HW_CFGMEM_TYPE/MEM_PART are set at creation. Before programming, the device must hold the flash-programming bitstream (create_hw_bitstream -hw_device ... [get_property PROGRAM.HW_CFGMEM_BITFILE ...]; program_hw_devices), which Vivado does automatically in the GUI flow.
tools.usage:
set cfg [current_hw_cfgmem]
set_property PROGRAM.ADDRESS_RANGE {use_file} $cfg
set_property PROGRAM.FILES [list ./top.mcs] $cfg
set_property PROGRAM.PRM_FILE ./top.prm $cfg
set_property PROGRAM.UNUSED_PIN_TERMINATION {pull-none} $cfg
set_property PROGRAM.BLANK_CHECK 0 $cfg
set_property PROGRAM.ERASE 1 $cfg
set_property PROGRAM.CFG_PROGRAM 1 $cfg
set_property PROGRAM.VERIFY 1 $cfg
set_property PROGRAM.CHECKSUM 0 $cfg
create_hw_bitstream -hw_device [current_hw_device] [get_property PROGRAM.HW_CFGMEM_BITFILE [current_hw_device]]
program_hw_devices [current_hw_device]
program_hw_cfgmem -hw_cfgmem $cfg

parameters.name: PROGRAM.FILES
parameters.description: Image file list; for -interface spix8 (dual QSPI) two files (_primary/_secondary).

parameters.name: PROGRAM.ADDRESS_RANGE
parameters.description: use_file or entire_device (erase/verify scope).

parameters.name: PROGRAM.ERASE / CFG_PROGRAM / VERIFY / CHECKSUM / BLANK_CHECK
parameters.description: Operation flags (1/0).

parameters.name: PROGRAM.UNUSED_PIN_TERMINATION
parameters.description: pull-none / pull-up / pull-down for the flash-programming bitstream's unused pins (keep board-safe).

parameters.name: PROGRAM.HW_CFGMEM_BITFILE (on hw_device)
parameters.description: Path of the internal indirect-programming bitstream for the selected flash.

tools.example:
# complete QSPI flow for a Kintex UltraScale board
write_cfgmem -format mcs -size 128 -interface SPIx4 -loadbit {up 0x0 ./top.bit} -force ./top.mcs
open_hw_manager; connect_hw_server; open_hw_target
current_hw_device [lindex [get_hw_devices xcku040*] 0]
create_hw_cfgmem -hw_device [current_hw_device] [lindex [get_cfgmem_parts {mt25qu01g-spi-x1_x2_x4}] 0]
set_property PROGRAM.FILES [list ./top.mcs] [current_hw_cfgmem]
set_property PROGRAM.PRM_FILE ./top.prm [current_hw_cfgmem]
set_property PROGRAM.ADDRESS_RANGE use_file [current_hw_cfgmem]
set_property PROGRAM.ERASE 1 [current_hw_cfgmem]; set_property PROGRAM.CFG_PROGRAM 1 [current_hw_cfgmem]; set_property PROGRAM.VERIFY 1 [current_hw_cfgmem]
create_hw_bitstream -hw_device [current_hw_device] [get_property PROGRAM.HW_CFGMEM_BITFILE [current_hw_device]]
program_hw_devices [current_hw_device]
program_hw_cfgmem -hw_cfgmem [current_hw_cfgmem]
boot_hw_device [current_hw_device]
tools.notes: get_cfgmem_parts lists supported flash devices (filter on the part name from the board schematic). After programming, boot_hw_device (or a board power cycle) makes the FPGA load from flash. delete_hw_cfgmem removes the object; readback_hw_cfgmem reads flash contents back to a file.

tools.name: get_cfgmem_parts / delete_hw_cfgmem / readback_hw_cfgmem / current_hw_cfgmem
tools.description: Supporting commands for flash programming: get_cfgmem_parts lists the configuration-memory part definitions Vivado knows (vendor, density, interface: spi-x1_x2_x4, spi-x8 dual, bpi-x16, ...) used as the argument to create_hw_cfgmem; current_hw_cfgmem selects/returns the active object on the device; readback_hw_cfgmem reads the flash contents into an .mcs/.bin file for archiving or comparison; delete_hw_cfgmem removes the object (e.g. to switch to a different flash part).
tools.usage:
get_cfgmem_parts [-regexp] [-nocase] [-filter <expr>] [-quiet] [<patterns>]
current_hw_cfgmem [-hw_device <dev>] [<hw_cfgmem>]
readback_hw_cfgmem [-checksum] [-force] [-format mcs|bin] [-offset <addr>] [-datacount <n>] [-file <out>] [-quiet] [-hw_cfgmem <obj>]
delete_hw_cfgmem [-quiet] <hw_cfgmem>

parameters.name: <patterns> for get_cfgmem_parts
parameters.description: e.g. {mt25qu256-spi-x1_x2_x4}, {s25fl512s-spi-x1_x2_x4}, {mt28gu01gaax1e-bpi-x16}; properties MEM_TYPE, MEM_DENSITY, MFR_NAME, DATA_WIDTH.

parameters.name: -offset / -datacount (readback)
parameters.description: Start address and byte count of the region to read.

parameters.name: -format
parameters.description: mcs or bin output.

tools.notes: The flash part list is per device family; a part missing from the list often has a compatible entry (same command set/density). Readback is slow over JTAG (tens of minutes for large flashes).

tools.name: boot_hw_device / readback_hw_device / verify_hw_devices
tools.description: Device-level operations beyond program_hw_devices: boot_hw_device issues a JTAG JPROGRAM so the device reconfigures from its non-volatile source (flash, after program_hw_cfgmem) without a power cycle; readback_hw_device reads the configuration memory of a running device into a .rbd/.bin file (with -readback_file/-bin_file) and optionally captures register state (-capture), used for verification, SEU checks and SEM analysis; verify_hw_devices compares the device's configuration against the programmed .bit and its .msk mask file (write_bitstream -mask_file) to confirm the bitstream loaded correctly.
tools.usage:
boot_hw_device [-disable_done_check] [-timeout <s>] [-quiet] <hw_device>
readback_hw_device [-force] [-capture] [-readback_file <f.rbd>] [-bin_file <f.bin>] [-quiet] <hw_device>
verify_hw_devices [-key efuse|bbram] [-verbose] [-quiet] <hw_devices>   ;# requires PROGRAM.FILE and a matching .msk next to it

parameters.name: -disable_done_check
parameters.description: Do not wait for DONE after boot (for designs with delayed DONE or Tandem PCIe).

parameters.name: -capture
parameters.description: Assert GCAPTURE before readback so flip-flop states are included.

parameters.name: -readback_file / -bin_file
parameters.description: ASCII (.rbd) or binary output of the readback data.

parameters.name: .msk
parameters.description: Mask file identifying the bits that verify should compare (excludes BRAM contents, etc.).

tools.example:
# after flashing: boot from QSPI and check DONE
boot_hw_device [current_hw_device]
puts [get_property REGISTER.IR.BIT5_DONE [current_hw_device]]
# verify a programmed bitstream
write_bitstream -force -mask_file ./top.bit   ;# generates top.msk beside top.bit
set_property PROGRAM.FILE ./top.bit [current_hw_device]
verify_hw_devices [current_hw_device]
# readback for SEU comparison
readback_hw_device -readback_file ./top_rb.rbd -bin_file ./top_rb.bin [current_hw_device]
tools.notes: Readback and verify are blocked for encrypted bitstreams (unless keys allow readback) and on devices with readback disabled by BITSTREAM.READBACK.SECURITY. Boot times out if the flash image is invalid; use -timeout for large images.

tools.name: write_hw_svf / execute_hw_svf
tools.description: Serial Vector Format generation: with a virtual SVF target open (create_hw_target, then open_hw_target as in the usage below), every JTAG operation performed (program_hw_devices, program_hw_cfgmem, boot, eFUSE) is recorded, and write_hw_svf writes it to an .svf file that any third-party JTAG tool or embedded controller can replay without Vivado; execute_hw_svf replays an .svf on a real target for validation. Used for production programming with non-AMD programmers and for boards where only a generic JTAG bridge is available.
tools.usage:
open_hw_manager
connect_hw_server
create_hw_target -copy [get_hw_targets */xilinx_tcf/Digilent/*] svf_target   ;# or create_hw_target svf_target with create_hw_device per chain member
open_hw_target [get_hw_targets */svf_target]
set_property PROGRAM.FILE ./top.bit [current_hw_device]
program_hw_devices [current_hw_device]
write_hw_svf -force ./program_top.svf
close_hw_target
# replay
open_hw_target [get_hw_targets */xilinx_tcf/Digilent/*]
execute_hw_svf ./program_top.svf

parameters.name: create_hw_target -copy
parameters.description: Clone the JTAG chain of a real target into a virtual SVF target so device order/IR lengths are correct.

parameters.name: create_hw_device -idcode -irlength -mask -part
parameters.description: Describe chain members manually when no real target is available.

parameters.name: write_hw_svf -force
parameters.description: Overwrite an existing file; the SVF accumulates all operations since the target was opened.

tools.example:
# Manual chain description for an offline SVF
create_hw_target my_svf
open_hw_target [get_hw_targets */my_svf]
create_hw_device -idcode 03822093 -irlength 6 -mask ffffffff -part xc7z020
set_property PROGRAM.FILE ./top.bit [current_hw_device]
program_hw_devices [current_hw_device]
write_hw_svf -force ./top.svf
tools.notes: SVF files for flash programming embed the flash-programming bitstream plus the whole image and can be very large; readback/verify results cannot be captured in SVF. The IDCODE for a part is in the device configuration user guide.

tools.name: get_hw_targets / close_hw_target / disconnect_hw_server / refresh_hw_target / set_property PARAM.FREQUENCY (JTAG clock)
tools.description: Target and server lifecycle: get_hw_targets lists the JTAG cables/targets a hw_server exposes (Digilent, Platform Cable, SmartLynq, XVC), each with properties such as UID, TYPE and PARAM.FREQUENCY (the TCK rate, changeable before open_hw_target to slow down flaky chains or speed up uploads), refresh_hw_target rescans the chain, close_hw_target releases the cable, disconnect_hw_server drops the server connection and close_hw_manager ends the session. get_hw_servers / current_hw_server handle multiple servers.
tools.usage:
get_hw_targets [-of_objects <hw_servers>] [-regexp] [-nocase] [-filter <expr>] [-quiet] [<patterns>]
set_property PARAM.FREQUENCY 15000000 [get_hw_targets */xilinx_tcf/Digilent/210308A1234]
open_hw_target [get_hw_targets */xilinx_tcf/Digilent/210308A1234]
refresh_hw_target [-quiet] [<hw_target>]
close_hw_target [-quiet] [<hw_target>]
disconnect_hw_server [-quiet] [<hw_server>]
close_hw_manager

parameters.name: PARAM.FREQUENCY
parameters.description: JTAG TCK in Hz (e.g. 6000000, 15000000, 30000000 depending on cable).

parameters.name: -filter on targets
parameters.description: e.g. {NAME =~ *Digilent*} or {UID == 210308A1234}.

parameters.name: current_hw_target
parameters.description: Select the open target when several are open.

tools.example:
open_hw_manager
connect_hw_server -url labpc:3121 -allow_non_jtag
foreach t [get_hw_targets] { puts "$t  [get_property TYPE $t] [get_property PARAM.FREQUENCY $t]" }
set t [get_hw_targets -filter {NAME =~ *SmartLynq*}]
set_property PARAM.FREQUENCY 30000000 $t
open_hw_target $t
current_hw_device [get_hw_devices xcvu9p_0]
# ...
close_hw_target
disconnect_hw_server
close_hw_manager
tools.notes: Long or noisy JTAG chains need lower TCK (start at 6 MHz). Device names are <part>_<index> in chain order; ARM DAP entries appear on Zynq. Tools > Auto Connect in the GUI performs open_hw_manager/connect/open_target on the first found cable.

tools.name: Xilinx Virtual Cable (XVC): open_hw_target -xvc_url and hw_server -e 'set auto-open-servers xilinx-xvc'
tools.description: XVC is a TCP protocol (default port 2542) that lets any device implementing the xvcServer commands (getinfo/settck/shift) act as a JTAG cable: an embedded Linux board driving its own PL JTAG through the debug bridge IP, a Raspberry Pi bit-banging JTAG, a PCIe card exposing XVC over the Debug Bridge (xvc_pcie driver), or a network JTAG adapter. Vivado connects either directly from the Hardware Manager with open_hw_target -xvc_url host:port, or by telling hw_server to auto-open the XVC server so the target appears in the normal list. This enables remote debug of deployed systems without a physical cable.
tools.usage:
open_hw_manager
connect_hw_server
open_hw_target -xvc_url 192.168.1.50:2542
# or make hw_server discover it
hw_server -e "set auto-open-servers xilinx-xvc:192.168.1.50:2542" -s tcp::3121
# then connect_hw_server -url localhost:3121 and the XVC target is listed by get_hw_targets

parameters.name: -xvc_url <host:port>
parameters.description: Address of the XVC server.

parameters.name: auto-open-servers xilinx-xvc:<host>:<port>
parameters.description: hw_server option to attach an XVC endpoint at start-up (comma-separated list for several).

parameters.name: Debug Bridge IP (debug_bridge)
parameters.description: C_DEBUG_MODE options: JTAG to BSCAN, AXI to BSCAN (XVC over AXI/PCIe), BSCAN to DebugHub, ... used on the device side.

tools.example:
# PCIe accelerator card: Debug Bridge (AXI to BSCAN) + xvc_pcie Linux driver (github.com/Xilinx/XilinxVirtualCable), then
open_hw_target -xvc_url server42:10200
set_property PROBES.FILE ./card.ltx [current_hw_device]
refresh_hw_device
# ILA/VIO work as with a physical cable
tools.notes: Bitstream programming over XVC is supported only when the XVC endpoint reaches the device's real JTAG TAP; through an AXI-based debug bridge only debug cores (not configuration) are reachable. Throughput depends on the XVC implementation's shift buffer size.

tools.name: report_hw_axi_txn / get_hw_axi_txns / delete_hw_axi_txn / reset_hw_axi / refresh_hw_axi
tools.description: Completing the JTAG-to-AXI Master flow: after create_hw_axi_txn defines a read or write burst and run_hw_axi executes it, report_hw_axi_txn prints the transaction's address, data and response (with -w for wide data formatting), get_hw_axi_txns lists the defined transactions and get_hw_axis the master cores, delete_hw_axi_txn removes definitions, reset_hw_axi resets the core's state machine after a hung transaction (e.g. an address with no slave) and refresh_hw_axi re-reads its status registers. This is the tool for peeking/poking AXI peripherals and memory from Tcl without software.
tools.usage:
get_hw_axis [-of_objects <hw_devices>] [-filter <expr>] [<patterns>]
create_hw_axi_txn [-address <hex>] [-data <hex>] [-size <bits>] [-len <beats>] [-type read|write] [-id <n>] [-burst incr|fixed|wrap] [-cache <n>] [-prot <n>] [-force] <name> <hw_axi>
run_hw_axi [-queue] [-quiet] <hw_axi_txns>
report_hw_axi_txn [-w <width>] [-t <type>] [-quiet] <hw_axi_txns>
get_hw_axi_txns [-of_objects <hw_axis>] [-filter <expr>] [<patterns>]
delete_hw_axi_txn [-quiet] <hw_axi_txns>
reset_hw_axi [-quiet] <hw_axis>
refresh_hw_axi [-quiet] <hw_axis>

parameters.name: -len / -size / -burst
parameters.description: Beats, beat size in bits (32/64/...), and burst type; data list length must equal len x size/32 words.

parameters.name: -queue (run)
parameters.description: Queue several transactions and execute them back to back.

parameters.name: -w (report)
parameters.description: Words per line in the data dump.

tools.example:
set axi [get_hw_axis hw_axi_1]
create_hw_axi_txn -force wr_ctrl $axi -type write -address 40000000 -len 1 -data 00000001
create_hw_axi_txn -force rd_stat $axi -type read  -address 40000004 -len 1
run_hw_axi wr_ctrl
run_hw_axi rd_stat
report_hw_axi_txn rd_stat
puts [get_property DATA [get_hw_axi_txns rd_stat]]
# 16-beat burst read of DDR
create_hw_axi_txn -force rd_ddr $axi -type read -address 80000000 -len 16 -size 32
run_hw_axi rd_ddr; report_hw_axi_txn -w 4 rd_ddr
tools.notes: Addresses are hexadecimal without 0x. The JTAG-to-AXI core's clock must be running and its reset released; a transaction to an unmapped address hangs until reset_hw_axi. The core supports AXI4 (full) and AXI4-Lite depending on its configuration.

tools.name: IBERT / Serial I/O Analyzer Tcl: get_hw_sio_gts, create_hw_sio_link, create_hw_sio_scan, run_hw_sio_scan, wait_on_hw_sio_scan, display_hw_sio_scan, write_hw_sio_scan
tools.description: Scripting the Serial I/O Analyzer on an IBERT core (IBERT UltraScale/UltraScale+/Versal, or the in-system IBERT integrated in the transceiver wizard): get_hw_sio_gts/get_hw_sio_txs/get_hw_sio_rxs/get_hw_sio_plls/get_hw_sio_commons enumerate the transceiver objects with their DRP-backed properties (line rate, loopback, TX pre/post-cursor, RX equaliser, PRBS pattern, error counters); create_hw_sio_link pairs a TX and RX into a link (or detect_hw_sio_links finds them automatically), set_property on the link sets pattern/loopback, create_hw_sio_scan defines a 1d_bathtub or 2d_full_eye scan on a link, run_hw_sio_scan / wait_on_hw_sio_scan execute it, display_hw_sio_scan shows the eye and write_hw_sio_scan saves it as CSV; create_hw_sio_sweep sweeps TX/RX settings across multiple scans. Used for link bring-up, margin qualification and production test.
tools.usage:
get_hw_sio_gts [-of_objects <hw_sio_iberts|links>] [-filter <expr>] [<patterns>]
create_hw_sio_link [-description <text>] [-quiet] <hw_sio_tx> <hw_sio_rx>
detect_hw_sio_links [-force] [-quiet]
set_property TX_PATTERN {PRBS 31-bit} <hw_sio_link>; set_property RX_PATTERN {PRBS 31-bit} <hw_sio_link>; set_property LOOPBACK {Near-End PMA} <hw_sio_link>
create_hw_sio_scan [-description <text>] [-quiet] 1d_bathtub|2d_full_eye <hw_sio_link|hw_sio_rx>
set_property HORIZONTAL_INCREMENT 2 <scan>; set_property VERTICAL_INCREMENT 2 <scan>; set_property DWELL_BER 1e-8 <scan>
run_hw_sio_scan [-quiet] <hw_sio_scans>
wait_on_hw_sio_scan [-timeout <min>] [-quiet] <hw_sio_scans>
display_hw_sio_scan [-quiet] <hw_sio_scans>
write_hw_sio_scan [-force] [-quiet] <file.csv> <hw_sio_scan>
read_hw_sio_scan <file.csv>
remove_hw_sio_scan <scans>; remove_hw_sio_link <links>

parameters.name: Link properties
parameters.description: TX_PATTERN/RX_PATTERN (PRBS 7/9/15/23/31-bit, Fast/Slow Clock), LOOPBACK (None, Near-End PCS/PMA, Far-End PCS/PMA), TXDIFFSWING, TX_PRE_CURSOR, TX_POST_CURSOR, RX_TERMINATION_VOLTAGE, RXLPMEN/DFE, RX_BER, RX_RECEIVED_BIT_COUNT, RX_BIT_ERROR_COUNT, LOGIC.ERRCNT_RESET (via set_property ... 1 + commit_hw_sio).

parameters.name: Scan properties
parameters.description: HORIZONTAL_INCREMENT, VERTICAL_INCREMENT, HORIZONTAL_RANGE (-100% .. 100%), VERTICAL_RANGE (100%), DWELL_BER or DWELL_TIME, SCAN_TYPE, OPEN_AREA / OPEN_PERCENTAGE results.

parameters.name: Sweeps
parameters.description: create_hw_sio_sweep with SWEEP properties enumerating TX/RX parameter sets; run_hw_sio_sweep / write_hw_sio_sweep.

tools.example:
open_hw_manager; connect_hw_server; open_hw_target
current_hw_device [get_hw_devices xcku040_0]
set_property PROGRAM.FILE ./ibert_example.bit [current_hw_device]
program_hw_devices; refresh_hw_device
set links [detect_hw_sio_links -force]
foreach l $links { set_property TX_PATTERN {PRBS 31-bit} $l; set_property RX_PATTERN {PRBS 31-bit} $l }
commit_hw_sio $links
set scan [create_hw_sio_scan -description "lane0 eye" 2d_full_eye [lindex $links 0]]
set_property HORIZONTAL_INCREMENT 4 $scan; set_property VERTICAL_INCREMENT 4 $scan; set_property DWELL_BER 1e-7 $scan
run_hw_sio_scan $scan
wait_on_hw_sio_scan -timeout 30 $scan
puts "open area: [get_property OPEN_AREA $scan]"
write_hw_sio_scan -force ./lane0_eye.csv $scan
tools.notes: Property changes on GT/link objects take effect after commit_hw_sio (the GUI does this on Apply); refresh_hw_sio re-reads counters. Eye scans require the RX equaliser in LPM or DFE mode matching the setup and are not supported on every 7 series transceiver type (see the UG908 device support table). IBERT designs are generated from the IP catalog (IBERT UltraScale) or the transceiver wizard's in-system IBERT option.

tools.name: set_property C_TRIGIN_EN / C_TRIGOUT_EN / C_ADV_TRIGGER / C_EN_STRG_QUAL / C_INPUT_PIPE_STAGES / C_NUM_OF_PROBES (debug core parameters)
tools.description: Parameters of an ILA debug core in the netlist-insertion flow (set on the debug_core object between create_debug_core and implement_debug_core; the IP flow sets the same through the ILA customization GUI): C_DATA_DEPTH (1024-131072 samples), C_TRIGIN_EN / C_TRIGOUT_EN add trigger-in/out ports for cross-triggering between ILAs or with a processor (Zynq cross-trigger), C_ADV_TRIGGER enables the advanced trigger state machine (up to 16 states, counters, flags), C_EN_STRG_QUAL enables storage (capture) qualification, C_INPUT_PIPE_STAGES (0-6) adds pipelining on probe inputs for timing closure, C_NUM_OF_PROBES counts the probe ports, and per-probe C_PROBEn_TYPE (0 data+trigger, 1 data only, 2 trigger only) / C_PROBEn_MU_CNT (match units) control comparator resources; the trigger mode itself is a run-time property, not a build parameter. The debug hub (dbg_hub) has C_CLK_INPUT_FREQ_HZ, C_ENABLE_CLK_DIVIDER and C_USER_SCAN_CHAIN.
tools.usage:
set core [create_debug_core u_ila_0 ila]
set_property C_DATA_DEPTH 8192 $core
set_property C_TRIGIN_EN true $core
set_property C_TRIGOUT_EN true $core
set_property C_ADV_TRIGGER true $core
set_property C_EN_STRG_QUAL true $core
set_property C_INPUT_PIPE_STAGES 2 $core
set_property ALL_PROBE_SAME_MU true $core
set_property ALL_PROBE_SAME_MU_CNT 2 $core
set_property C_CLK_INPUT_FREQ_HZ 200000000 [get_debug_cores dbg_hub]
set_property C_ENABLE_CLK_DIVIDER false [get_debug_cores dbg_hub]

parameters.name: C_DATA_DEPTH
parameters.description: Samples per probe set; BRAM cost = depth x total probe width.

parameters.name: C_TRIGIN_EN / C_TRIGOUT_EN
parameters.description: Create trig_in/trig_in_ack and trig_out/trig_out_ack ports (connect with connect_debug_port ... trig_in etc.).

parameters.name: C_ADV_TRIGGER
parameters.description: Advanced trigger state machine (.tsm scripts loaded via CONTROL.TRIGGER_STATE_MACHINE_FILE at run time).

parameters.name: C_EN_STRG_QUAL
parameters.description: Capture qualification support (CONTROL.CAPTURE_MODE BASIC).

parameters.name: C_INPUT_PIPE_STAGES
parameters.description: 0-6 register stages on probes.

parameters.name: ALL_PROBE_SAME_MU / ALL_PROBE_SAME_MU_CNT / C_PROBEn_MU_CNT
parameters.description: Number of match units (comparators) per probe, 1-16; more allow multiple compare values per probe in advanced triggers.

tools.example:
# Cross trigger two ILAs: ILA A's trig_out into ILA B's trig_in
connect_debug_port u_ila_a/trig_out    [get_nets xtrig_a2b]
connect_debug_port u_ila_b/trig_in     [get_nets xtrig_a2b]
connect_debug_port u_ila_b/trig_in_ack [get_nets xtrig_a2b_ack]
connect_debug_port u_ila_a/trig_out_ack [get_nets xtrig_a2b_ack]
implement_debug_core
# at run time
set_property CONTROL.TRIG_OUT_MODE TRIGGER_ONLY [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]
set_property CONTROL.TRIGGER_MODE TRIG_IN_ONLY  [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_2]
tools.notes: Parameters cannot be changed after implement_debug_core without re-running implementation. In block designs the same options are on the ILA/System ILA IP (Trigger In/Out Ports, Advanced Trigger, Capture Control, Input Pipe Stages). Zynq PS cross-trigger uses the CTI ports of the processing_system7/zynq_ultra_ps_e IP.

tools.name: Advanced trigger state machine (.tsm) and CONTROL.TRIGGER_STATE_MACHINE_FILE
tools.description: When an ILA was built with C_ADV_TRIGGER, the trigger can be a small state machine written in the Trigger State Machine language: up to 16 states with if/elseif/else conditions on probe compares ($counter, $flag objects; probe operators ==, !=, <, >, transitions R/F/B/N), actions goto, trigger, increment/reset counters, set/clear flags, and 4 counters with configurable widths. The file is loaded at run time with CONTROL.TRIGGER_STATE_MACHINE_FILE and TRIGGER_MODE ADVANCED_ONLY, making it possible to trigger on sequences (e.g. 'third write after a read timeout') that basic AND/OR compares cannot express.
tools.usage:
set_property CONTROL.TRIGGER_MODE ADVANCED_ONLY [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]
set_property CONTROL.TRIGGER_STATE_MACHINE_FILE ./seq_trigger.tsm [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]
run_hw_ila [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]

parameters.name: state <name>: ... ;
parameters.description: State definitions; the first state is the initial one.

parameters.name: if (<cond>) then ... elseif ... else ... endif
parameters.description: Conditions on probes: (probe_name == 8'hA5), (probe_name == 1'bR), counters ($counter0 == 16'u10).

parameters.name: goto <state> / trigger / increment_counter $counterN / reset_counter / set_flag $flagN / clear_flag
parameters.description: Actions.

parameters.name: Counters
parameters.description: $counter0..$counter3 with widths configured in the Trigger Setup window before running.

tools.notes: Syntax and limits (max states, counters, flags) are in UG908 'Trigger State Machine Language'. Basic mode compare values are ignored while the state machine is active. The GUI's Trigger Setup window has a .tsm editor with syntax checking.

tools.name: Trigger at startup (apply_hw_ila_trigger + write_bitstream)
tools.description: Capturing events right after configuration (reset sequences, boot handshakes) is done by arming the ILA before programming: open the implemented design, configure the ILA's run-time trigger settings in the Hardware Manager on a previously programmed device with the same design, export those settings with 'Trigger at Startup' (which writes them into the design as ILA properties via the hw_ila -> debug core property transfer: apply_hw_ila_trigger, or the GUI's 'Set Trigger at Startup' in the ILA dashboard), regenerate the bitstream with write_bitstream, and the ILA is then armed as soon as the device configures; connecting the Hardware Manager afterwards and refreshing shows the captured data.
tools.usage:
# 1. in hardware: set trigger conditions, positions, depth on hw_ila_1 as usual
# 2. transfer them to the open implemented design (same design/netlist must be open in this Vivado session)
apply_hw_ila_trigger [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]
# 3. regenerate
write_bitstream -force ./top_trig_at_startup.bit
# 4. program, connect, refresh_hw_device -> the captured data uploads

parameters.name: apply_hw_ila_trigger
parameters.description: Copies the hw_ila run-time settings into the debug core's trigger-at-startup parameters of the open design (or a specified .ila/.tsm).

parameters.name: GUI
parameters.description: The 'Set Trigger at Startup' action in the Hardware Manager ILA dashboard, available while the matching implemented design is open.

tools.example:
open_run impl_1
open_hw_manager; connect_hw_server; open_hw_target
set_property PROGRAM.FILE ./top.bit [current_hw_device]; set_property PROBES.FILE ./top.ltx [current_hw_device]
program_hw_devices; refresh_hw_device
set ila [get_hw_ilas hw_ila_1]
set_property TRIGGER_COMPARE_VALUE eq1'bR [get_hw_probes boot_done -of_objects $ila]
set_property CONTROL.TRIGGER_POSITION 512 $ila
apply_hw_ila_trigger $ila
write_bitstream -force ./top_tas.bit
set_property PROGRAM.FILE ./top_tas.bit [current_hw_device]; program_hw_devices; refresh_hw_device
upload_hw_ila_data $ila; display_hw_ila_data
tools.notes: Only the bitstream changes; no re-implementation. The armed ILA starts capturing at end of configuration, so the first samples reflect GSR release. Details and GUI steps are in UG908 'Trigger at Startup'.

tools.name: Netlist insertion vs. HDL instantiation debug flows (ILA/System ILA/Debug Hub)
tools.description: Two ways to add debug cores: (1) netlist insertion, where MARK_DEBUG nets in the synthesized design are connected to ILA cores created by the Set Up Debug wizard or create_debug_core/connect_debug_port Tcl, stored as debug constraints in the XDC (create_debug_core lines) and implemented by implement_debug_core; the debug hub is inserted automatically and the flow keeps RTL untouched; (2) HDL instantiation, where the ILA/VIO/System ILA IP from the catalog (or in a block design) is instantiated like any IP with explicit probe connections, which survives synthesis changes and lets a block design's System ILA monitor whole AXI interfaces with protocol-aware waveforms; in both cases write_debug_probes produces the .ltx and the hardware flow is identical. The debug hub (dbg_hub) connects all cores to BSCAN and must run at a clock that is free-running and constrained (C_CLK_INPUT_FREQ_HZ for JTAG timing).
tools.usage:
# insertion flow (post-synthesis)
open_run synth_1
set_property MARK_DEBUG true [get_nets -hier {u_ctrl/state[*] u_ctrl/start}]
create_debug_core u_ila_0 ila
set_property C_DATA_DEPTH 2048 [get_debug_cores u_ila_0]
set_property port_width 1 [get_debug_ports u_ila_0/clk]
connect_debug_port u_ila_0/clk [get_nets clk_100]
create_debug_port u_ila_0 probe
set_property port_width 4 [get_debug_ports u_ila_0/probe0]
connect_debug_port u_ila_0/probe0 [get_nets {u_ctrl/state[0] u_ctrl/state[1] u_ctrl/state[2] u_ctrl/state[3]}]
save_constraints
implement_debug_core
# instantiation flow: create_ip -name ila / system_ila in a BD, connect probes in RTL/BD

parameters.name: MARK_DEBUG
parameters.description: Attribute (RTL or XDC) that preserves a net through synthesis for insertion; also shows the net in the Set Up Debug wizard.

parameters.name: Set Up Debug wizard
parameters.description: Flow Navigator > Synthesized Design > Set Up Debug: pick nets, clock domains, depth, trigger/capture options; writes the create_debug_core constraints.

parameters.name: System ILA (system_ila)
parameters.description: Block-design IP that probes AXI interfaces and nets with interface-aware display (transactions decoded in the waveform) and optional protocol checker.

parameters.name: write_debug_probes / PROBES.FILE
parameters.description: .ltx generation (automatic with write_bitstream) and loading in the Hardware Manager.

tools.example:
# Remove insertion-flow debug cores from a design
delete_debug_core [get_debug_cores -filter {NAME != dbg_hub}]
delete_debug_core [get_debug_cores dbg_hub]
save_constraints
# or in block designs: delete the system_ila cell and 'Mark Debug' annotations
tools.notes: Insertion-flow debug constraints reference synthesized net names and break when the RTL changes; the XDC usually needs regeneration. Debug cores add BRAM and routing; remove them (or set the ILA's probes to fewer bits) before final timing sign-off, or keep them and re-verify timing. Versal adds ChipScoPy (Python) as an alternative client for ILA/VIO/IBERT/DDRMC over the hw_server.

tools.name: ChipScoPy (Python API for Versal debug)
tools.description: Open-source Python client library (pip install chipscopy; github.com/Xilinx/chipscopy) that connects to hw_server and cs_server (the ChipScope server that must run alongside hw_server for Versal) to program a PDI and drive the debug cores of Versal devices from Python: ILA (trigger setup, run, upload, waveform export), VIO, IBERT/eye scans, DDR memory controller calibration/margin status (DDRMC), NoC performance monitoring, System Monitor readings and PCIe link status. It complements the Tcl Hardware Manager, particularly for automated lab tests and Jupyter-based analysis.
tools.usage:
from chipscopy import create_session, report_versions
session = create_session(hw_server_url="TCP:localhost:3121", cs_server_url="TCP:localhost:3042")
device = session.devices.filter_by(family="versal").get()
device.program("design.pdi")
device.discover_and_setup_cores(ltx_file="design.ltx")
ila = device.ila_cores.get(name="design_1_i/axi_ila")
ila.set_probe_trigger_value("s_axi_awvalid", "eq", 1)
ila.run_basic_trigger(window_count=1, window_size=1024, trigger_position=256)
ila.wait_till_done(max_wait_minutes=1)
ila.upload()
waveform = ila.waveform; waveform.export_waveform("csv", "capture.csv")

parameters.name: create_session(hw_server_url, cs_server_url)
parameters.description: Connect to the two servers (cs_server default port 3042).

parameters.name: device.program(pdi) / device.discover_and_setup_cores(ltx_file=...)
parameters.description: Program and enumerate debug cores.

parameters.name: ila_cores / vio_cores / ibert_cores / ddr_cores / noc_core / sysmon_root / pcie_cores
parameters.description: Core collections with per-core APIs.

parameters.name: cs_server
parameters.description: Executable shipped with Vivado (Vivado Lab included) that ChipScoPy talks to; hw_server handles JTAG.

tools.example:
# Start the servers on the lab machine
$ hw_server -s TCP::3121 &
$ cs_server -s TCP::3042 &
# Then run the Python script above; examples/ in the chipscopy repository cover ILA, VIO, IBERT, DDR, SysMon and NoC.
tools.notes: ChipScoPy versions track Vivado releases (e.g. chipscopy 2024.2 with Vivado 2024.2); mismatched versions fail on connect. It targets Versal only; 7 series/UltraScale debug remains Tcl/GUI (or XVC/third-party tools).

tools.name: vivado_lab (Vivado Lab Edition)
tools.description: A small standalone installation (no synthesis/implementation) that contains only the Hardware Manager, the Tcl shell, hw_server/cs_server and the programming tools, for lab and production machines: it programs devices and flash, runs ILA/VIO/IBERT/SysMon dashboards, opens .ila captures and executes the same hardware Tcl commands as full Vivado. Started as vivado_lab (GUI) or vivado_lab -mode tcl/batch -source script.tcl.
tools.usage: vivado_lab [-mode gui|tcl|batch] [-source <script.tcl>] [-log <f>] [-journal <f>] [-tclargs ...]

parameters.name: -mode batch -source
parameters.description: Headless programming scripts on production stations.

parameters.name: Included tools
parameters.description: hw_server, cs_server and the Hardware Manager Tcl/GUI; program_flash, xsdb and bootgen ship with Vitis, not with Lab Edition.

tools.example:
vivado_lab -mode batch -source program_board.tcl -tclargs ./top.bit
# program_board.tcl
open_hw_manager; connect_hw_server; open_hw_target
current_hw_device [lindex [get_hw_devices] 0]
set_property PROGRAM.FILE [lindex $argv 0] [current_hw_device]
program_hw_devices [current_hw_device]
close_hw_manager
tools.notes: Free, no license needed. Version should match the Vivado that built the .ltx/.bit for full debug-core compatibility (older Lab Editions cannot read newer .ltx formats).

tools.name: .bit / .bin / .rbt (bitstream formats)
tools.description: Configuration bitstream files from write_bitstream for 7 series, UltraScale and UltraScale+: .bit has a header (design name, part, date) followed by the configuration data and is what program_hw_devices and the Hardware Manager consume; .bin (write_bitstream -bin_file) is the raw data without header for flash images, PCAP/ICAP loading by software (Zynq fpga_manager, xdevcfg) and third-party loaders; .rbt (-raw_bitfile) is the ASCII '0'/'1' rendering for tools that need text. Compression (BITSTREAM.GENERAL.COMPRESS TRUE), encryption/authentication (BITSTREAM.ENCRYPTION.*), per-frame CRC and the config-interface settings (SPI bus width, CONFIGRATE) are baked into all three formats.
tools.usage: write_bitstream -force [-bin_file] [-raw_bitfile] [-mask_file] [-readback_file] [-logic_location_file] [-no_partial_bitfile] [-cell <rp_cell>] [-reference_bitfile <f>] <file.bit>

parameters.name: -bin_file
parameters.description: Also write <name>.bin (headerless).

parameters.name: -raw_bitfile
parameters.description: Also write <name>.rbt (ASCII).

parameters.name: -mask_file
parameters.description: Write <name>.msk for verify_hw_devices.

parameters.name: -readback_file / -logic_location_file
parameters.description: .rbd expected readback and .ll frame/bit location map for readback tools.

parameters.name: -no_partial_bitfile / -cell
parameters.description: DFX: skip or select partial bitstreams.

tools.example:
set_property BITSTREAM.GENERAL.COMPRESS TRUE [current_design]
set_property BITSTREAM.CONFIG.SPI_BUSWIDTH 4 [current_design]
set_property BITSTREAM.CONFIG.CONFIGRATE 33 [current_design]
write_bitstream -force -bin_file ./top.bit
# Zynq Linux: byte order for fpga_manager is the .bin as written by Vivado 2016+ (earlier tools needed bootgen -process_bitstream bin)
tools.notes: The .bit header makes the file ~100 bytes larger than the .bin; a .bit in flash will not boot. Zynq-7000 requires the .bin (or bootgen-processed) bitstream for PCAP loading with correct byte order. Versal uses .pdi instead (write_device_image).

tools.name: .mcs / .prm / .bin (configuration memory images from write_cfgmem)
tools.description: Flash images produced by write_cfgmem: .mcs is Intel-HEX style (with extended addressing) and is the traditional format for the Hardware Manager and third-party programmers; .bin is the raw binary image of the flash (used by embedded update mechanisms and by program_hw_cfgmem on some parts); .prm is a small text map listing the address ranges occupied by each loaded file (bitstream(s), data) that the Hardware Manager uses for use_file programming and verification. Options set the flash size in MB (-size), the interface (spix1/spix2/spix4/spix8, bpix8/bpix16, smapx8/x16/x32), the load points (-loadbit 'up <addr> <bit>' and -loaddata 'up <addr> <file>'), checksum and dual-quad splitting (spix8 produces _primary/_secondary files).
tools.usage: write_cfgmem -format mcs|bin -size <MB> -interface spix1|spix2|spix4|spix8|bpix8|bpix16|smapx8|smapx16|smapx32|serialx1 [-loadbit {up <addr> <file.bit> [up <addr> <file2.bit>]}] [-loaddata {up <addr> <file.bin>}] [-checksum] [-disablebitswap] [-verbose] [-force] <output>

parameters.name: -size
parameters.description: Flash size in megabytes (e.g. 16, 32, 64, 128, 256).

parameters.name: -interface
parameters.description: Configuration interface and bus width matching the board and BITSTREAM.CONFIG.SPI_BUSWIDTH.

parameters.name: -loadbit / -loaddata
parameters.description: One or more bitstreams / arbitrary data files at flash offsets ('up' = ascending).

parameters.name: -checksum
parameters.description: Print the image checksum for production records.

parameters.name: -disablebitswap
parameters.description: Keep bit order for interfaces that swap (e.g. some BPI/SelectMAP loaders).

tools.example:
# Multiboot: golden image at 0, update image at 0x01000000, plus a data blob
write_cfgmem -format mcs -size 32 -interface SPIx4 \
  -loadbit {up 0x00000000 ./golden.bit up 0x01000000 ./update.bit} \
  -loaddata {up 0x01F00000 ./calibration.bin} -checksum -force ./flash_image.mcs
# dual QSPI (x8)
write_cfgmem -format mcs -size 256 -interface SPIx8 -loadbit {up 0x0 ./top.bit} -force ./top.mcs   ;# writes top_primary.mcs / top_secondary.mcs
tools.notes: The bitstream's own BITSTREAM.CONFIG.NEXT_CONFIG_ADDR / CONFIGFALLBACK properties define the multiboot jump. -size must be at least the sum of loaded content; the Hardware Manager rejects images larger than the selected flash part.

tools.name: .ltx (debug probes file)
tools.description: The probes file that describes every debug core in a bitstream (ILA, VIO, JTAG-to-AXI, IBERT, System ILA, debug bridge) with their hub addresses, the probe names, widths, types, enumerations and the interface metadata that lets System ILA decode AXI transactions. Written by write_debug_probes or automatically next to the .bit by write_bitstream, and loaded in the Hardware Manager with set_property PROBES.FILE (or FULL_PROBES.FILE for the complete list including partial-reconfiguration modules) followed by refresh_hw_device; Vivado auto-loads a .ltx that sits beside the PROGRAM.FILE with the same base name.
tools.usage:
write_debug_probes [-no_partial_ltxfile] [-cell <rp_cell>] [-force] [-quiet] <file.ltx>
set_property PROBES.FILE ./top.ltx [current_hw_device]
set_property FULL_PROBES.FILE ./top_full.ltx [current_hw_device]   ;# DFX designs
refresh_hw_device [current_hw_device]

parameters.name: PROBES.FILE
parameters.description: Probe file for the currently loaded configuration.

parameters.name: FULL_PROBES.FILE
parameters.description: Superset .ltx covering all reconfigurable modules; the active subset is selected per RM.

parameters.name: -cell / -no_partial_ltxfile
parameters.description: DFX: write per-RM or skip partial probe files.

tools.example:
# after implementation
open_run impl_1
write_debug_probes -force ./debug/top.ltx
# hardware
set_property PROGRAM.FILE ./top.bit [current_hw_device]
set_property PROBES.FILE  ./debug/top.ltx [current_hw_device]
program_hw_devices; refresh_hw_device
get_hw_ilas; get_hw_vios
tools.notes: A mismatched .ltx (from a different implementation) shows cores with wrong probe names or 'unable to find core' errors; always pair the .ltx with the exact .bit. The file is XML and can be inspected to see probe-to-net mappings.

tools.name: .msk / .rbd / .ll / .svf / .pdi (readback, verify, vector and Versal image formats)
tools.description: Auxiliary programming files: .msk (write_bitstream -mask_file) marks which configuration bits are meaningful for verify_hw_devices (BRAM/LUTRAM contents masked out); .rbd (-readback_file) is the expected readback data and .ll (-logic_location_file) maps frame/bit positions to flip-flops and BRAM bits so readback (readback_hw_device) can be decoded (used for SEU injection, state capture, SEM classification with .ebd/.ebc essential-bit files); .svf (write_hw_svf) is the vendor-neutral JTAG vector file; .pdi (write_device_image) is the Versal Programmable Device Image, a bootgen-style container of PLM, boot header, PL CFI data, NoC/AIE configuration and optional ELFs, programmed with program_hw_devices exactly like a .bit or written to flash/SD as BOOT.BIN by bootgen.
tools.usage:
write_bitstream -force -mask_file -readback_file -logic_location_file ./top.bit   ;# top.msk, top.rbd, top.ll
set_property BITSTREAM.SEU.ESSENTIALBITS yes [current_design]     ;# also writes top.ebd/.ebc for SEM
write_device_image -force ./top.pdi                                ;# Versal
set_property PROGRAM.FILE ./top.pdi [current_hw_device]; program_hw_devices

parameters.name: .msk
parameters.description: Same size as the .bit; 1 = bit is compared by verify.

parameters.name: .ll
parameters.description: Text: one line per element with frame address, bit offset, block type and net/cell name.

parameters.name: .ebd / .ebc
parameters.description: Essential bits data (ASCII) and count for SEM classification of upsets.

parameters.name: .pdi
parameters.description: Versal image; bootgen -arch versal builds boot images (BOOT.BIN) from it and the software components.

tools.example:
# Versal: bootable image with Linux components
bootgen -arch versal -image boot.bif -o BOOT.BIN -w on
# boot.bif
all: { image { { type=bootimage, file=./top.pdi } } image { name=apu_ss, id=0x1c000000 { type=raw, load=0x1000, file=system.dtb } { core=a72-0, exception_level=el-3, trustzone, file=bl31.elf } { core=a72-0, exception_level=el-2, file=u-boot.elf } } }
tools.notes: Readback/logic-location workflows are described in UG908 'Readback' and XAPP1261; SEM in PG187/PG036 and Versal XilSEM docs. .pdi files are release-specific: the PLM in the PDI must match the Vivado/Vitis version's runtime expectations.

tools.name: Program Device / Program Configuration Memory Device / Add Configuration Memory Device (Hardware Manager GUI)
tools.description: The Hardware Manager's right-click and Flow Navigator actions: Open Target (Auto Connect / Open New Target wizard with local or remote server, selection of cable and JTAG frequency), Program Device (dialog for the .bit/.pdi and optional .ltx; programs and refreshes), Add Configuration Memory Device (pick the flash part with filters for manufacturer/density/width; asks to program immediately), Program Configuration Memory Device (image files, .prm, address range, erase/program/verify/checksum checkboxes), Boot from Configuration Memory Device, Readback Device, Verify Device, Program eFUSE Registers / Program BBR Key (security keys), Refresh Device, Export SVF file (when an SVF target is open), plus the per-core dashboards (ILA, VIO, IBERT, SysMon, JTAG-to-AXI) opened from the Hardware window tree.
tools.usage: Flow Navigator > Program and Debug > Open Hardware Manager > Open Target > Auto Connect; Hardware window: right-click device > Program Device... / Add Configuration Memory Device... / Program Configuration Memory Device... / Boot from Configuration Memory Device / Readback Device / Verify Device / Program eFUSE Registers... / Program BBR Key...

parameters.name: Program Device dialog
parameters.description: Bitstream file, Debug probes file, Enable end of startup check, Program (echoes set_property PROGRAM.FILE/PROBES.FILE + program_hw_devices + refresh_hw_device).

parameters.name: Add Configuration Memory Device dialog
parameters.description: Search by part name; sets create_hw_cfgmem with the chosen get_cfgmem_parts entry.

parameters.name: Hardware Device Properties
parameters.description: Shows REGISTER.* (IDCODE, STATUS, BOOTSTS, USR_ACCESS, EFUSE.*), PROGRAM.*, PROBES.FILE and the flash object.

parameters.name: Dashboard windows
parameters.description: Settings/Status/Trigger Setup/Capture Setup/Waveform for ILA; VIO Cores probes table; Serial I/O Links/Scans; SysMon plots.

tools.example:
1. Open Hardware Manager > Open Target > Auto Connect
2. Right-click xc7z020_1 > Program Device > select top.bit and top.ltx > Program
3. Right-click device > Add Configuration Memory Device > filter 'n25q128' > OK > 'Do you want to program the configuration memory device now?' Yes
4. Configuration file top.mcs, PRM top.prm, Address Range Configuration File Only, Erase/Program/Verify > OK
5. Right-click > Boot from Configuration Memory Device
tools.notes: Every dialog echoes its Tcl to the console, which is the quickest way to script a lab procedure. The Hardware window shows the JTAG chain; devices greyed out are not programmable from this session (e.g. Arm DAP entries).
